verdicts.quote: Expose a Lightning Web Component (LWC) through a Salesforce custom tab labeled Grok Bot. Put it in an existing suitable Lightning app's navigation
Set sharing explicitly and perform no business-record queries or writes.
The bot does not automatically add Salesforce user identifiers, CRM fields, or secrets to the request.
Keep the tab access, Apex class permission and external credential principal mapping in a dedicated least-privilege permission set.
No user sees another user's draft, result or operation status.

Inapplicable service concerns include cache invalidation, delta cursors, subscriptions, durable queues and background job recovery for chat, since each send is a bounded request/response with a transient view.
verdicts.missing: The callout-after-DML and no-callout-from-trigger constraints are never stated, and the design is synchronous, not asynchronous (Queueable/future/batch).

verdicts.quote: The underlying secret is entered only via approved administrative credential setup, stored in protected server-side custody... The browser and product source, logs and handoff never contain credential values.
Salesforce documents a 120-second cumulative Apex callout ceiling and a 6 MB synchronous callout request/response ceiling with heap implications.
verdicts.missing: Numbers for callouts per transaction, heap size and CPU time.

verdicts.quote: Use controlled fixtures that vary model output and failure shape
verdicts.missing: That Apex tests cannot make real callouts and need a mock callout implementation (HttpCalloutMock).

verdicts.quote: Use an enhanced Salesforce Named Credential linked to a Custom External Credential with a named principal.
verdicts.missing: That the api.x.ai host must be registered as the Named Credential URL or Remote Site, or the callout is refused.

verdicts.quote: associate each promise with the active view and attempt so late results cannot rehydrate conversation state
verdicts.missing: The reply comes back inline from an imperative Apex promise. No async notification mechanism (platform event, polled status, LMS) is given.

verdicts.quote: Retry resubmits that prompt once with the same completed context and reuses its visible message. ... No automatic retry and no fabricated reply.
The integration owner must establish the supported attempt deadline and overload behavior on the chosen model and target runtime before live readiness.
verdicts.missing: Concrete concurrent-request limits and what the user sees when a request cannot be accepted because of capacity.

verdicts.quote: A timeout, network loss, throttle, upstream service failure or unusable response shows a persistent, sanitized error with Retry available. Invalid or missing configuration shows a contact-admin action.
verdicts.missing: Timeout and 5xx get the same user outcome. A generic 4xx refusal (e.g. 400/content rejection) is not separately specified.

verdicts.quote: A timeout, network loss, throttle... shows a persistent, sanitized error with Retry available... No automatic retry
A failed, nonterminal, incomplete or empty upstream response produces no assistant message and follows R-3.
Prompt and reply text are displayed only to the current user and held in active view memory plus request processing. The bot neither stores them durably
The provider receives only the submitted text and permitted in-view context plus model/request controls... instructs them to use synthetic, non-sensitive content.
If the context exceeds the confirmed budget, decline the send before dispatch and offer Clear conversation to start fresh.
verdicts.missing: The size of the context budget. It is left open.

verdicts.quote: Empty or whitespace-only text shows a validation cue and triggers no outbound call... Numeric limits remain open below.
An authorized operator can distinguish a successful completion, local rejection, access/configuration failure, timeout, throttling and upstream failure
verdicts.missing: An explicit admin control to turn the bot off, and how an admin changes the model (the model is only server-selected deployable config).

verdicts.quote: Org creation, production deployment and general staff access are outside this request.
verdicts.missing: How configuration and credentials differ per environment, and the production code-coverage requirement.

verdicts.quote: Pending always reaches reply or actionable failure within the confirmed request deadline.
verdicts.missing: The deadline/latency value itself. It is left open.

verdicts.quote: Both themes share consistent type and spacing scales, semantic palettes, one icon set and designed empty, pending, error and reply states.
No domain records, object permissions, field permissions or sharing rules are changed.
